title.en: The Right It: Why So Many Ideas Fail and How to Make Sure Yours Succeed
title.zh: 做对的事：为什么如此多的想法会失败，以及如何确保你的想法成功

category.zh: 创业 · 商业 · 产品

one_liner.en: Most new products fail not because they were *built wrong* but because they were **The Wrong It**—nobody wanted them. The cure is not better thinking but **your own real-world data with skin in the game**: pretend you have the product (*pretotype*), put it in front of the market cheaply and fast, and let the data—not opinions—tell you whether to build it.
one_liner.zh: 大多数新产品失败，不是因为**做得不对**，而是因为它做的是**错的东西**——根本没人想要。解药不是更聪明地思考，而是**带着真金白银投入的、你亲手收集的真实市场数据**：假装你已经有了产品（*预型 pretotype*），用极低的成本和极快的速度把它推到市场面前，让数据——而非意见——告诉你该不该真的去造它。

body_md.en:
Savoia—a three-time startup winner who then got blindsided by a $25M, five-year, flawlessly-executed failure—sets out to answer one question: *if everything was done right, why did we still fail?* His answer reframes the entire problem of building new things.

**The problem:** ~80–90% of all new products fail in the market, *even when competently executed*. He calls this the **Law of Market Failure**, and treats it as a hard, permanent fact, not a motivational obstacle. The dominant cause of failure is not bad engineering or bad marketing—it's **Premise**: the idea was simply something not enough people wanted. You built **The Wrong It**.

**The core claim:** You cannot *think* your way to knowing whether an idea will succeed. Opinions—yours, your friends', even experts'—are nearly worthless predictors, because they're formed in *Thoughtland* (the realm of abstract speculation) with no real consequences attached. The only reliable signal is **YODA: Your Own DAta**, collected firsthand from the real market, *with skin in the game* (people risking money, time, or reputation).

**Why read it:** It gives you a cheap, fast, repeatable engineering method—**pretotyping**—to test demand *before* you invest, so you stop wasting years and millions discovering that the market never wanted your beautifully-built product. The mantra: **Make sure you are building The Right It before you build It right.**
body_md.zh:
萨沃亚——一位连续三次创业成功、随后却被一次耗资 2500 万美元、历时五年、执行无懈可击的失败彻底击垮的人——试图回答一个问题：*如果一切都做对了，我们为什么还是失败了？* 他的答案重构了“做新东西”这件事的整个问题框架。

**问题所在：** 约 80%–90% 的新产品在市场上失败，*即便执行得非常出色*。他称之为**市场失败定律（Law of Market Failure）**，并把它当作一个坚硬、永久的事实，而非一个靠励志就能跨越的障碍。失败最主要的原因不是糟糕的工程或糟糕的营销，而是**前提（Premise）**：这个想法压根就不是足够多的人想要的东西。你造的是**错的东西（The Wrong It）**。

**核心主张：** 你无法靠*思考*得知一个想法会不会成功。意见——你的、朋友的、甚至专家的——几乎毫无预测价值，因为它们诞生于*思想国（Thoughtland）*（抽象臆测的领域），不附带任何真实后果。唯一可靠的信号是 **YODA：你自己的数据（Your Own DAta）**，亲手从真实市场采集，并且*带着切身投入（skin in the game）*（人们押上了金钱、时间或声誉）。

**为何值得读：** 它给了你一套廉价、快速、可重复的工程方法——**预型法（pretotyping）**——让你在投入*之前*就检验需求，从而不再浪费数年和数百万，最后才发现市场从来不想要你精心打造的产品。其箴言是：**在把东西做对之前，先确保你做的是对的东西。**

body_md.en:
The book is built as a three-stage argument that mirrors its three parts: first *diagnose the disease* (why ideas die), then *hand you the instruments* (tools to test cheaply), then *teach bedside manner* (tactics + a full worked case). Everything hangs off one diagnosis and one cure.

```mermaid
mindmap
  root(("The Right It"))
    Part I - Hard Facts
      Law of Market Failure
        80 to 90 percent fail
        Fail even if well executed
      Success Equation
        All factors must be right
        One wrong factor equals fail
      The Right It vs The Wrong It
        Premise is the root cause
      Thoughtland trap
        Opinions are not data
        Four Trolls
        False positives and negatives
      Data beats Opinions
        OPD is not enough
        Collect YODA
    Part II - Sharp Tools
      Thinking Tools
        Market Engagement Hypothesis
        Say it with Numbers
        XYZ Hypothesis
        Hypozooming to xyz
      Pretotyping Tools
        Pretotype not Prototype
        Mechanical Turk
        Pinocchio
        Fake Door and Facade
        YouTube
        One Night Stand
        Infiltrator and Relabel
      Analysis Tools
        Skin in the Game Caliper
        TRI Meter
    Part III - Plastic Tactics
      Think globally test locally
      Testing now beats later
      Think cheap cheaper cheapest
      Tweak and flip before quit
      Worked example - BusU
```

**The internal logic:** Part I establishes that the enemy (failure) is *statistical and structural*, then locates its true source (wrong Premise, not bad execution), then explains *why we keep choosing The Wrong It* (we trust Thoughtland opinions). This creates a precise need: real market data, collected by us, with consequences attached. Part II then supplies exactly that, in a pipeline—**clarify the idea (thinking tools) → test it without building it (pretotyping tools) → interpret the result objectively (analysis tools)**. Part III is the operating discipline that keeps the pipeline cheap, fast, and local, plus a single example (BusU) that runs an idea through the entire machine. Each part exists *only because* the previous part created a gap it must fill.

**内在逻辑：** 第一部分先确立敌人（失败）是*统计性、结构性*的，再定位其真正源头（错误的前提，而非糟糕的执行），再解释*我们为何总在选错的东西*（我们相信思想国的意见）。这就制造出一个精确的需求：由我们亲手采集、附带后果的真实市场数据。第二部分恰好供给这一点，形成一条流水线——**澄清想法（思维工具）→ 不造产品就检验它（预型工具）→ 客观解读结果（分析工具）**。第三部分是让这条流水线保持廉价、快速、本地化的操作纪律，外加一个实例（BusU）把一个想法完整跑过整台机器。每一部分的存在，*都仅仅因为*前一部分制造了一个它必须填补的缺口。

body_md.en:
The book is one long deductive chain. Each link forces the next; if you accept the premises, the method is the only rational conclusion.

**Premise 1 — Failure is the default, structurally.** Success requires *many* key factors to all turn out right simultaneously: `Right A × Right B × Right C × … = Success`. It's multiplicative, like multiplying by zero—a *single* wrong factor zeroes the whole product. If an outcome depends on *n* factors, there are 2ⁿ–1 ways to fail and only 1 way to succeed. Nielsen data confirms it: ~80% of new products fail, year after year, across every industry. → **Failure is the most likely outcome.**

**Premise 2 — Competence doesn't save you.** Coca-Cola (New Coke), Google (Wave, Glass), Disney (John Carter) are world-class and still fail constantly. Interviewing failures (the **FLOP** taxonomy: Failure due to **L**aunch, **O**perations, or **P**remise) revealed that once you strip away the blame-game, the dominant root cause is **Premise**—the idea was The Wrong It. → *The bottleneck is not how you build, but what you build.*

**Premise 3 — You can't think your way to the answer.** Ideas marinated in *Thoughtland* attract opinions, not facts. Four cognitive trolls corrupt them: **Lost-in-Translation** (others picture your idea differently), **Prediction** (humans are terrible at forecasting their own future behavior), **No-Skin-in-the-Game** (free opinions cost nothing, so mean nothing), and **Confirmation Bias** (we cherry-pick evidence). Result: false positives (Webvan—$800M on a 'sure thing' nobody actually bought) and false negatives (Uber, Airbnb, the Ring doorbell—all dismissed as stupid). → *Opinions are unreliable in both directions.*

**Premise 4 — Therefore you need data, but a specific kind.** Not **OPD** (Other People's Data—stale, irrelevant, untrustworthy, drawn from other times/places/methods), which fails the four data tests (freshness, relevance, known provenance, statistical significance). You need **YODA: Your Own DAta**, collected firsthand, that passes all four tests *and* carries **skin in the game**—the person gave up something real (money > time > validated phone > validated email; opinions/likes = zero).

**The mechanism (the cure) — Pretotyping.** But you can't collect market data on a product that doesn't exist yet (chicken-and-egg). The escape is to *pretend* the product exists and measure the market's real response—the IBM speech-to-text experiment (a hidden human typist faked the AI) is the prototype-of-the-idea. This is cheaper and faster than building, and it answers the *only* question that matters early: not 'Can we build it?' (prototype's question) but **'Should we build it?'**

**Conclusion.** Run multiple cheap pretotyping experiments, score each on the TRI Meter against your numeric hypotheses, accumulate enough YODA to overpower the Law-of-Market-Failure prior, and *then* decide: go, tweak, or drop. The whole book is the proof that this is the rational response to Premises 1–4.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Idea for a new product"] --> B{"Built right but failed?"}
  B -->|"~80-90% of cases"| C["It was The Wrong It - wrong Premise"]
  C --> D["Why did we choose it? We trusted Thoughtland opinions"]
  D --> E["Four Trolls corrupt opinions"]
  E --> F["False positives and false negatives"]
  F --> G["Need DATA not opinions"]
  G --> H{"Whose data?"}
  H -->|"OPD - others' data"| I["Insufficient - fails the 4 tests"]
  H -->|"YODA - your own data"| J["Reliable IF it has skin in the game"]
  J --> K["But product does not exist yet"]
  K --> L["Pretotype: pretend it exists, test cheaply and fast"]
  L --> M["Collect YODA with skin in the game"]
  M --> N["Score on TRI Meter vs XYZ hypothesis"]
  N --> O{"Enough positive evidence?"}
  O -->|"Yes"| P["The Right It - build it right"]
  O -->|"Mixed"| Q["Tweak and flip, retest"]
  O -->|"No"| R["Drop it - saved time and money"]
  Q --> L
```
body_md.zh:
全书是一条长长的演绎链。每一环都逼出下一环；只要你接受前提，这套方法就是唯一理性的结论。

**前提一 —— 失败在结构上就是默认结果。** 成功要求*许多*关键要素同时全部为真：`对的A × 对的B × 对的C × … = 成功`。它是乘法式的，就像乘以零——*一个*错误要素就会把整个乘积归零。若一个结果取决于 *n* 个要素，则有 2ⁿ–1 种失败方式，而只有 1 种成功方式。Nielsen 的数据印证了这一点：约 80% 的新产品失败，年复一年，横跨所有行业。→ **失败是最可能的结果。**

**前提二 —— 能力救不了你。** 可口可乐（新可乐）、谷歌（Wave、Glass）、迪士尼（《异星战场》）都是世界顶级，却仍不断失败。访谈失败者（**FLOP** 分类法：失败源于**发布 L**aunch、**运营 O**perations 或**前提 P**remise）揭示出：剥去互相甩锅之后，主导性的根因是**前提**——这个想法是错的东西。→ *瓶颈不在于你怎么造，而在于你造什么。*

**前提三 —— 你无法靠思考得到答案。** 在*思想国*里腌泡过久的想法吸引的是意见，不是事实。四只认知小妖会败坏它们：**翻译走样**（别人脑中的画面和你不同）、**预测失灵**（人类极不擅长预测自己未来的行为）、**无切身投入**（免费意见不付代价，所以毫无意义）、**确认偏误**（我们专挑支持自己的证据）。结果就是假阳性（Webvan——为一个“稳赢”却没人真买的点子烧掉 8 亿美元）和假阴性（Uber、Airbnb、Ring 门铃——全被斥为愚蠢）。→ *意见在两个方向上都不可靠。*

**前提四 —— 因此你需要数据，但是特定的那种。** 不是 **OPD**（别人的数据——陈旧、不相关、不可信，来自别的时间/地点/方法），它过不了四项数据检验（新鲜度、相关性、来源清楚、统计显著）。你需要的是 **YODA：你自己的数据**，亲手采集，能通过全部四项检验，*并且*带着**切身投入**——这个人放弃了真实的东西（金钱 > 时间 > 验证过的电话 > 验证过的邮箱；意见/点赞 = 零）。

**机制（解药）—— 预型法。** 但你无法在一个尚不存在的产品上采集市场数据（鸡生蛋问题）。出路是*假装*产品已存在，并测量市场的真实反应——IBM 语音转文字实验（隐藏的人类打字员假扮 AI）就是“想法的雏形”。这比真造便宜、快，而且回答了早期*唯一*重要的问题：不是“我们能造出来吗？”（原型的问题），而是**“我们该不该造？”**

**结论。** 跑多个廉价的预型实验，用 TRI 仪表对照你的数字化假设给每个打分，累积足够多的 YODA 以压过“市场失败定律”这个先验，*然后*再决定：上、微调、还是放弃。整本书就是在证明：这是对前提一至四的理性回应。

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["一个新产品想法"] --> B{"造得很对却失败了?"}
  B -->|"约八到九成的情形"| C["它是错的东西 - 前提错了"]
  C --> D["我们为何选了它? 因为信了思想国的意见"]
  D --> E["四只小妖败坏意见"]
  E --> F["假阳性与假阴性"]
  F --> G["需要数据而非意见"]
  G --> H{"谁的数据?"}
  H -->|"OPD 别人的数据"| I["不够 - 过不了四项检验"]
  H -->|"YODA 你自己的数据"| J["可靠 前提是带切身投入"]
  J --> K["但产品还不存在"]
  K --> L["预型: 假装它存在 廉价快速地测"]
  L --> M["采集带切身投入的 YODA"]
  M --> N["用 TRI 仪表对照 XYZ 假设打分"]
  N --> O{"正面证据足够吗?"}
  O -->|"够"| P["对的东西 - 把它造对"]
  O -->|"参半"| Q["微调并翻转 重测"]
  O -->|"不够"| R["放弃 - 省下时间和钱"]
  Q --> L
```

body_md.en:
### 1. The Law of Market Failure & the Success Equation
`Right A × Right B × Right C × … = Success`. Success is *multiplicative*: every key factor must be right; one wrong factor (×0) collapses the outcome. With *n* factors there are 2ⁿ–1 ways to fail, 1 to succeed. This is the mathematical reason failure (~80%) is the default—and the logic later used to *beat* it (find and fix the one factor that matters most: Premise).

### 2. The Right It vs. The Wrong It
- **The Right It** = an idea that, *if competently executed*, **will** succeed in the market.
- **The Wrong It** = an idea that, *even if competently executed*, **will** fail.
The distinction is about Premise (does the market want it?), which execution cannot fix. *More* effort on The Wrong It just makes the failure bigger.

### 3. Thoughtland & the Four Trolls
Thoughtland = the abstract mental space where ideas attract opinions instead of facts.

| Troll | What it corrupts | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Lost-in-Translation | Communication of the idea | Others imagine a different product |
| Prediction | Self-forecasting | People can't predict their own behavior |
| No-Skin-in-the-Game | Validity of the signal | Free opinions are worthless |
| Confirmation Bias | Interpretation | We keep only flattering evidence |

Produces **false positives** (Webvan) and **false negatives** (Uber, Airbnb, Ring).

### 4. OPD vs. YODA, and the four data tests
Good data must pass: **Freshness · Relevance · Known Provenance · Statistical Significance**.
- **OPD** (Other People's Data) fails ≥1 test → insufficient, never a substitute.
- **YODA** (Your Own DAta) = firsthand, passes all four, *with skin in the game*.

### 5. The Thinking-Tools pipeline: MEH → XYZ → xyz
- **MEH (Market Engagement Hypothesis):** a one-sentence statement of how you assume the market will engage. Usually too fuzzy.
- **Say it with Numbers → XYZ Hypothesis:** `At least X% of Y will Z` (X = % of market, Y = target market, Z = the engagement action). De-fuzzes vague words and surfaces hidden disagreements (the Stanford pollution-sensor example: '"some people in polluted cities" → "≥10% of people in cities with AQI>100 will buy a $120 sensor"').
- **Hypozooming → xyz:** zoom XYZ down to a small, local, testable-*now* subset (Y→y). If XYZ is true, xyz must be true—but xyz is testable today (e.g., 'Beijing Tot Academy parents').

### 6. Pretotyping vs. Prototyping (the central tool)
One vowel, two purposes.

| | Prototype | Pretotype |
|---|---|---|
| Question | **Can** we build it? Will it work? | **Should** we build it? Will they want it? |
| Cost / time | Weeks–years, $$$ | Hours–days, ~$0–hundreds |
| Output | A working artifact | YODA with skin in the game |

**A pretotype must:** (1) produce YODA *with skin in the game*, (2) be implemented *quickly*, (3) be implemented *cheaply*.

**The pretotype catalog** (mix & combine freely):

| Pretotype | Core move | Canonical example |
|---|---|---|
| Mechanical Turk | Hide a human behind 'tech' you can't build yet | IBM speech-to-text; Fold4U folding machine |
| Pinocchio | A non-functional mock-up you *pretend* is real | Hawkins' wooden PalmPilot; the bean-can smart speaker 'HAL' |
| Fake Door | A front door (ad/site) to count interest; nothing behind it | Kevin Kelly's $1 catalog ad; SquirrelWatching.com |
| Facade | Like Fake Door, but you *actually deliver* | CarsDirect sold 4 real cars with zero inventory |
| YouTube | A video of the not-yet-built product + a skin-in-the-game ask | Google Glass Explorer program ($1,500) |
| One-Night Stand | A one-shot/short-run offer, no long commitment | Virgin Airlines' first chartered flight; Airbnb's 3 air mattresses |
| Infiltrator | Sneak your product into someone else's store | Walhub disguised as IKEA 'Wälhub' |
| Relabel | Re-label an existing product to test a new one | Second-Day Sushi stickers |

### 7. The Skin-in-the-Game Caliper
Scores market responses by what they *cost* the giver. Orders of magnitude, not false precision.

| Evidence | Points |
|---|---|
| Opinions, encouragement, likes, comments, surveys, fake email | **0** |
| Validated email (knowingly given) | 1 |
| Validated phone number | 10 |
| Time (attend a demo) | 1 pt / minute |
| Cash deposit / order | 1 pt / dollar |

*'Money talks, opinion walks.'* In 'A Tale of Two Teams,' Team A's 140,000 views = 0 points; Team B's 80 emails + 20 orders = thousands of points of real signal.

### 8. The TRI Meter (The Right It Meter)
A 5-band gauge—**Very Unlikely (10%) · Unlikely (30%) · 50/50 · Likely (70%) · Very Likely (90%)**—onto which you map each experiment by asking: *'If this idea is The Right It, how likely is it that this experiment would have produced this result?'* A permanent **black 'Law of Market Failure' arrow** points at Very Unlikely: your idea is presumed 'guilty' (The Wrong It) until enough YODA proves otherwise. You need ~3–5+ experiments (more for bigger bets); one experiment is never enough.
body_md.zh:
### 1. 市场失败定律与成功方程式
`对的A × 对的B × 对的C × … = 成功`。成功是*乘法式*的：每个关键要素都得对；一个错误要素（×0）就让结果崩塌。有 *n* 个要素时，有 2ⁿ–1 种失败方式，只有 1 种成功方式。这就是失败（约 80%）成为默认结果的数学原因——也是后文用来*战胜*它的逻辑（找到并修正最关键的那个要素：前提）。

### 2. 对的东西 vs. 错的东西
- **对的东西** = 一个想法，*若执行得当*，**将会**在市场上成功。
- **错的东西** = 一个想法，*即便执行得当*，**也将**失败。
二者之别在于前提（市场想不想要它），而前提是执行无法弥补的。在错的东西上投入*越多*，失败只会越大。

### 3. 思想国与四只小妖
思想国 = 想法吸引意见而非事实的抽象心理空间。

| 小妖 | 它败坏什么 | 后果 |
|---|---|---|
| 翻译走样 | 想法的传达 | 别人想象的是另一个产品 |
| 预测失灵 | 自我预测 | 人无法预测自己的行为 |
| 无切身投入 | 信号的有效性 | 免费意见一文不值 |
| 确认偏误 | 解读 | 我们只留下讨好自己的证据 |

它会产生**假阳性**（Webvan）和**假阴性**（Uber、Airbnb、Ring）。

### 4. OPD vs. YODA，以及四项数据检验
好数据必须通过：**新鲜度 · 相关性 · 来源清楚 · 统计显著**。
- **OPD**（别人的数据）至少有一项不过关 → 不够，永远不能替代。
- **YODA**（你自己的数据）= 亲手采集，四项全过，*且带切身投入*。

### 5. 思维工具流水线：MEH → XYZ → xyz
- **MEH（市场参与假设）：** 一句话说明你假设市场会如何参与。通常太模糊。
- **用数字说话 → XYZ 假设：** `至少 X% 的 Y 会 Z`（X = 市场百分比，Y = 目标市场，Z = 参与动作）。它把含糊词去模糊化，并让隐藏的分歧浮出水面（斯坦福污染传感器案例：“污染城市里的一些人” → “AQI>100 的城市里至少 10% 的人会买一台 120 美元的传感器”）。
- **缩放假设 → xyz：** 把 XYZ 缩小到一个小的、本地的、*现在就能测*的子集（Y→y）。若 XYZ 为真，xyz 必为真——但 xyz 今天就能测（如”北京 Tot 幼儿园的家长”）。

### 6. 预型 vs. 原型（核心工具）
一个元音之差，两种目的。

| | 原型 Prototype | 预型 Pretotype |
|---|---|---|
| 问题 | 我们**能**造吗？它管用吗？ | 我们**该不该**造？他们会想要吗？ |
| 成本/时间 | 数周至数年，巨额 | 数小时至数天，约 0 到几百元 |
| 产出 | 一个可用的实物 | 带切身投入的 YODA |

**一个预型必须：**（1）产出*带切身投入*的 YODA，（2）能*快速*实现，（3）能*廉价*实现。

**预型清单**（可自由混搭组合）：

| 预型 | 核心招数 | 经典案例 |
|---|---|---|
| 机械土耳其人 | 在造不出的”技术”背后藏一个人 | IBM 语音转文字；Fold4U 叠衣机 |
| 匹诺曹 | 一个你*假装*是真的非功能模型 | 霍金斯的木头 PalmPilot；豆罐头智能音箱”HAL” |
| 假门 | 一扇前门（广告/网站）计数兴趣，门后空无一物 | 凯文·凯利 1 美元目录广告；SquirrelWatching.com |
| 门面 | 像假门，但你*真的交付* | CarsDirect 零库存卖出 4 辆真车 |
| YouTube | 一段尚未造出产品的视频 + 一个切身投入的要求 | 谷歌 Glass 探索者计划（1500 美元） |
| 一夜情 | 一次性/短期的报价，不做长期承诺 | 维珍航空第一架包机；Airbnb 的三张气垫床 |
| 渗透者 | 把你的产品偷偷塞进别人的店里 | 伪装成宜家”Wälhub“的 Walhub |
| 换标 | 给现有产品换个标签来测新产品 | “隔夜寿司”贴纸 |

### 7. 切身投入卡尺
按市场反应对给出者的*代价*打分。用数量级，不要假精确。

| 证据 | 分数 |
|---|---|
| 意见、鼓励、点赞、评论、问卷、假邮箱 | **0** |
| 验证过的邮箱（自愿给出） | 1 |
| 验证过的电话号码 | 10 |
| 时间（来听一场演示） | 1 分/分钟 |
| 现金押金 / 下单 | 1 分/美元 |

*“钱会说话，意见走开。”* 在”两个团队的故事”里，A 队的 14 万次观看 = 0 分；B 队的 80 个邮箱 + 20 笔订单 = 数千分的真实信号。

### 8. TRI 仪表（The Right It 仪表）
一个五档刻度盘——**极不可能(10%) · 不可能(30%) · 五五开 · 可能(70%) · 极可能(90%)**——你把每个实验映射上去，方法是问：*“如果这个想法是对的东西，这个实验产生这个结果的可能性有多大？”* 一个永久的**黑色”市场失败定律”箭头**指向”极不可能”：在足够多的 YODA 证明之前，你的想法被推定”有罪”（是错的东西）。你需要约 3–5 个以上的实验（赌注越大越多）；单个实验永远不够。

body_md.en:
### Prelude & Overview
Savoia's $25M, five-year, flawlessly-executed startup failure—despite a 3-and-0 prior record—becomes the wound the book heals. Even he 'did everything right' and still got bitten by 'the Beast of Failure.' He even *pretotyped this very book*: a 5-day stapled booklet (*Pretotype It!*, 2011) whose viral demand proved a real book was The Right It. Terminology: *product*/*It* = any new product, service, business, or initiative; *market* = anyone you hope will engage with it.

### Part I — Hard Facts
**Ch 1 · The Law of Market Failure.** 'Failure is not an option' is a lie; *failure is the most likely outcome*. The Law: **most new products fail, even if competently executed** (~80% per Nielsen, year after year). The **Success Equation** (multiplicative; one ×0 ruins it) explains *why*. Competence is no shield: New Coke, John Carter, Google Wave all failed under expert hands. The **FLOP** taxonomy (Launch / Operations / **Premise**) locates the true culprit: **Premise**—you built The Wrong It. Mantra introduced: *Make sure you are building The Right It before you build It right.*

**Ch 2 · The Right It.** Defines The Right It / The Wrong It (execution can't rescue a wrong Premise). Why we keep picking The Wrong It: **Thoughtland**, where ideas attract opinions like barnacles. The hocus-pocus **focus group** (LadyLike beer) shows research done in Thoughtland lies. The **Four Trolls** (Lost-in-Translation, Prediction, No-Skin, Confirmation Bias) generate **false positives** (Webvan: ~$800M) and **false negatives** (Uber, Airbnb, Tesla Roadster, the Ring doorbell rejected on *Shark Tank*). You can't tell true from false signals in Thoughtland—so escape it.

**Ch 3 · Data Beats Opinions.** Google's principle. But not *any* data: it must be **fresh, relevant, of known provenance, statistically significant** ('anecdotes are not data'). **OPD** (Other People's Data) fails these—five scenarios show why a similar idea's success/failure tells you almost nothing about yours. The cure: **YODA, Your Own DAta**, collected firsthand. An ounce of YODA beats a ton of OPD.

### Part II — Sharp Tools
**Ch 4 · Thinking Tools.** Fuzzy thinking feeds failure. The **MEH** (Market Engagement Hypothesis) names your core assumption ('If there's no market, there's no way'; 'If there's a market, there's a way'). **Say it with Numbers** turns belief into a testable claim. The **XYZ Hypothesis** (`≥X% of Y will Z`) de-fuzzes it and surfaces hidden disagreements. **Hypozooming** shrinks XYZ → a small, local, testable-now *xyz* (world → Beijing → one preschool). But you still have no product—so you're stuck… until pretotyping.

**Ch 5 · Pretotyping Tools.** The **IBM speech-to-text** story births the word: a hidden typist faked an AI no one could build, revealing users would *not* actually want it. **Pretotype ≠ Prototype**: prototype answers *Can we build it?*; pretotype answers *Should we?*—cheaply, in hours. The full catalog with examples: **Mechanical Turk** (IBM, Fold4U), **Pinocchio** (wooden PalmPilot, bean-can 'HAL'), **Fake Door** (Kevin Kelly's $1 ad, squirrel-book site; note the ethics caveat), **Facade** (CarsDirect's 4 real cars), **YouTube** (Google Glass Explorer), **One-Night Stand** (Virgin, Airbnb, Tesla pop-up), **Infiltrator** (Walhub/Wälhub in IKEA), **Relabel** (Second-Day Sushi). Three requirements: YODA-with-skin, quick, cheap.

**Ch 6 · Analysis Tools.** Data needs interpretation. The **Skin-in-the-Game Caliper** scores responses by cost to the giver (opinions/likes = 0; email = 1; phone = 10; time = 1/min; money = 1/$). 'A Tale of Two Teams': vanity metrics (140k views = 0) vs. real signal (80 emails + 20 orders). The **TRI Meter** maps each experiment to a likelihood band, anchored by the black Law-of-Market-Failure arrow; you need 3–5+ experiments, tweaking the idea (Ideas 1→5) until arrows cluster at Likely/Very Likely.

### Part III — Plastic Tactics
**Ch 7 · Tactics Toolkit.** *Plastic* = plasticity ('Everybody has a plan until I punch them in the mouth'—Tyson). **(1) Think globally, test locally** → minimize **Distance to Data (DTD)**. **(2) Testing now beats testing later** → minimize **Hours to Data (HTD)**; fear of rejection keeps us in Thoughtland. **(3) Think cheap, cheaper, cheapest** → minimize **Dollars to Data ($TD)** ('Creativity loves constraints'). **(4) Tweak it and flip it before you quit it** → The Right It is often a few tweaks away (Second-Day Sushi → Superior Sushi, via Tina Seelig's assumption-flipping). *Ten tiny tweaks beat one painful pivot.*

**Ch 8 · Complete Example: BusU.** 'Take a class on the bus.' The entire machine, end to end: idea → MEH → XYZ (`≥2% of pros with 1hr+ commutes will pay $3,000 for a 10-week class`) → three xyz hypotheses scored by DTD/HTD/$TD → cheapest first (Fake-Door website to Google commuters). Reality punches back: people want pricing clarity; Google won't subsidize; the $3,000/10-week idea dies (Idea 1) but a $300/1-week AI class sells out (Idea 2), with a lucky break (a volunteer instructor). Final YODA: 22% paid $300, 48% repeat, 0% bought the long course—~$40,000 of skin in the game. *Before writing a business plan, make sure there is a business.*

### Ch 9 · Final Words
Recaps the hard facts, sharp tools, plastic tactics in a single sequence. **Three promises:** (1) you'll cut failure odds dramatically (flip ~80% fail → ~80% succeed, *if* you then execute well); (2) even if you fail, you won't feel like a fool (you played the odds right); (3) if you stick with it, you'll eventually succeed (10–20% *do* win; it's like card-counting—keep collecting YODA and the odds tilt your way). Closes with the bigger question: now that you can find The Right It, *is it The Right It for **you**, and for **the world**?*
body_md.zh:
### 前奏与概览
萨沃亚那次耗资 2500 万、历时五年、执行无懈可击的创业失败——尽管此前战绩 3 胜 0 负——成了本书要疗愈的伤口。连他都”什么都做对了”，仍被”失败之兽”咬中。他甚至*为这本书本身做了预型*：一本 5 天装订成册的小册子（《Pretotype It!》，2011），其病毒式的需求证明了真正的书是对的东西。术语：*产品*/*It* = 任何新产品、服务、企业或倡议；*市场* = 任何你希望去参与它的人。

### 第一部分 —— 硬事实
**第 1 章 · 市场失败定律。**“失败不是一个选项”是谎言；*失败才是最可能的结果*。定律：**大多数新产品会失败，即便执行得当**（据 Nielsen 约 80%，年复一年）。**成功方程式**（乘法式；一个 ×0 就毁掉全局）解释了*为什么*。能力并非护盾：新可乐、《异星战场》、谷歌 Wave 都在专家之手下失败。**FLOP** 分类法（发布/运营/**前提**）锁定真凶：**前提**——你造的是错的东西。本书箴言登场：*在把东西做对之前，先确保你做的是对的东西。*

**第 2 章 · 对的东西。** 定义对的东西/错的东西（执行救不了错误的前提）。我们为何总选错的东西：**思想国**，想法在那里像藤壶一样吸附意见。变魔术般的**焦点小组**（LadyLike 啤酒）展示了在思想国做的调研会说谎。**四只小妖**（翻译走样、预测失灵、无切身投入、确认偏误）制造**假阳性**（Webvan：约 8 亿美元）和**假阴性**（Uber、Airbnb、特斯拉 Roadster，以及在《创智赢家》上被否的 Ring 门铃）。在思想国你分不清真假信号——所以要逃离它。

**第 3 章 · 数据胜过意见。** 谷歌的原则。但不是*任何*数据：它必须**新鲜、相关、来源清楚、统计显著**（”轶事不是数据”）。**OPD**（别人的数据）过不了这几关——五种情景说明一个相似想法的成败几乎无法告诉你关于你自己想法的任何事。解药：**YODA，你自己的数据**，亲手采集。一盎司 YODA 胜过一吨 OPD。

### 第二部分 —— 锋利工具
**第 4 章 · 思维工具。** 模糊的思考喂养失败。**MEH**（市场参与假设）点明你的核心假设（”没有市场，就没有路”；”有市场，就有路”）。**用数字说话**把信念变成可检验的主张。**XYZ 假设**（`至少 X% 的 Y 会 Z`）将其去模糊化并让隐藏分歧浮现。**缩放假设**把 XYZ 缩成一个小的、本地的、现在就能测的 *xyz*（世界 → 北京 → 一所幼儿园）。但你仍然没有产品——于是卡住了……直到预型法出现。

**第 5 章 · 预型工具。** **IBM 语音转文字**的故事催生了这个词：隐藏的打字员假扮了一个无人能造的 AI，揭示用户其实*并不*真想要它。**预型 ≠ 原型**：原型回答*我们能造吗？*；预型回答*我们该不该？*——廉价、几小时内完成。带案例的完整清单：**机械土耳其人**（IBM、Fold4U）、**匹诺曹**（木头 PalmPilot、豆罐头”HAL“）、**假门**（凯文·凯利 1 美元广告、松鼠书网站；注意伦理告诫）、**门面**（CarsDirect 的 4 辆真车）、**YouTube**（谷歌 Glass 探索者）、**一夜情**（维珍、Airbnb、特斯拉快闪店）、**渗透者**（宜家里的 Walhub/Wälhub）、**换标**（隔夜寿司）。三项要求：带切身投入的 YODA、快、便宜。

**第 6 章 · 分析工具。** 数据需要解读。**切身投入卡尺**按给出者的代价为反应打分（意见/点赞 = 0；邮箱 = 1；电话 = 10；时间 = 1/分；金钱 = 1/美元）。”两个团队的故事”：虚荣指标（14 万次观看 = 0）对比真实信号（80 个邮箱 + 20 笔订单）。**TRI 仪表**把每个实验映射到某个可能性档位，以黑色的”市场失败定律”箭头作锚；你需要 3–5 个以上的实验，不断微调想法（想法 1→5），直到箭头聚集在”可能/极可能”。

### 第三部分 —— 弹性战术
**第 7 章 · 战术工具箱。** *Plastic* = 可塑性（”每个人都有计划，直到我一拳打在他嘴上”——泰森）。**(1) 全局思考，本地检验** → 最小化**到数据的距离（DTD）**。**(2) 现在测胜过以后测** → 最小化**到数据的小时数（HTD）**；对被拒的恐惧让我们困在思想国。**(3) 想便宜、更便宜、最便宜** → 最小化**到数据的金钱（$TD）**（”创意热爱约束”）。**(4) 先微调再翻转，然后才放弃** → 对的东西往往只差几次微调（隔夜寿司 → 高端寿司，借助蒂娜·西利格的”假设翻转”法）。*十次小微调胜过一次痛苦的转向。*

**第 8 章 · 完整实例：BusU。**“在公交车上上一堂课。”整台机器，从头到尾：想法 → MEH → XYZ（`至少 2% 单程通勤 1 小时以上的职场人愿付 3000 美元上一门十周课`）→ 用 DTD/HTD/$TD 给三个 xyz 假设打分 → 先测最便宜的（面向谷歌通勤者的假门网站）。现实回击：人们想要清晰的定价；谷歌不补贴；3000 美元/十周的想法死掉（想法 1），但 300 美元/一周的 AI 课售罄（想法 2），还撞上好运（一位志愿讲师）。最终 YODA：22% 付了 300 美元，48% 复购，0% 买长课——约 4 万美元的切身投入。*在写商业计划书之前，先确保真的有一门生意。*

### 第 9 章 · 结语
把硬事实、锋利工具、弹性战术汇成一条序列。**三个承诺：**（1）你会大幅降低失败几率（把约 80% 失败翻转成约 80% 成功，*前提*是你随后执行得好）；（2）即使失败，你也不会觉得自己是傻瓜（你赌对了概率）；（3）只要坚持，你终将成功（10–20% *确实*会赢；这像算牌——持续采集 YODA，胜算就向你倾斜）。以更大的问题收尾：既然你已能找到对的东西，*它对**你**是对的东西吗？对**世界**呢？*

body_md.en:
> **Make sure you are building The Right It before you build It right.**

> Most new products will fail in the market, even if competently executed. *(The Law of Market Failure)*

> No amount of competent execution—brilliant design, clever engineering, impeccable quality, masterful marketing, or superior salesmanship—can save a product that is based on the wrong Premise.

> You cannot determine if an idea is The Right It just through thinking. Not through your thoughts. Not through the thoughts and opinions of others. Not through the thoughts of 'experts.'

> Opinions about an idea are not data—not even close.

> An ounce of YODA is worth a ton of OPD.

> If there's no market, there's no way. … If there's a market, there's a way.

> Prototypes help us answer the key question: *Can we build it?* Pretotypes, in contrast, answer a very different question: *Should we build it?*

> Before you put a lot of skin in the game on your idea, make sure you can get some skin in the game from your target market.

> Money talks, opinion walks.

> Ten tiny tweaks are better than one painful pivot.

> Test a little before you invest a lot.

> Before writing a business plan, make sure that there is a business.
body_md.zh:
> **在把东西做对之前，先确保你做的是对的东西。**

> 大多数新产品都会在市场上失败，即便执行得当。*（市场失败定律）*

> 再出色的执行——精妙的设计、巧妙的工程、无瑕的品质、高超的营销或卓越的销售——都救不了一个建立在错误前提之上的产品。

> 你无法仅凭思考就判定一个想法是不是对的东西。不能凭你的思考，不能凭别人的思考与意见，也不能凭”专家”的思考。

> 关于一个想法的意见不是数据——差得远。

> 一盎司 YODA 抵得上一吨 OPD。

> 没有市场，就没有路。……有市场，就有路。

> 原型帮我们回答关键问题：*我们能造出来吗？* 而预型回答的是一个截然不同的问题：*我们该不该造？*

> 在你为自己的想法押上大量切身投入之前，先确保你能从目标市场那里换来一些切身投入。

> 钱会说话，意见走开。

> 十次小微调胜过一次痛苦的转向。

> 在投入很多之前，先小小地测一下。

> 在写商业计划书之前，先确保真的有一门生意。

body_md.en:
Savoia is refreshingly self-aware (he even labels his own examples 'OPD' and 'anecdotal'), but an INTP should still press on the load-bearing joints.

**1. Survivorship bias in the evidence base.** Almost every cited success (Airbnb, Virgin, PalmPilot, CarsDirect, The Martian) is reconstructed *after* it won—'these had a cheap early test, therefore the test caused the win.' But we never see the graveyard of products that *passed* their pretotypes and still failed, or that *failed* a pretotype yet would have succeeded at scale. The method's hit-rate is asserted ('80ish percent guaranteed'), never measured. By his own standard, the book's central claim lacks YODA.

**2. The pretotype/market mismatch is under-examined.** A pretotype tests a *proxy* signal in a *local* slice. It can be a great false-negative *and* false-positive machine when the proxy diverges from the real product: Google Glass passed an expensive skin-in-the-game test ($1,500 + travel) and *still* flopped—Savoia admits initial commitment ≠ sustained engagement, but offers no systematic way to know in advance which products need a *retention* pretotype vs. a *first-purchase* one. Curiosity-buys (Fold4U's 'tried it once') vs. real demand is exactly the boundary that's hard to read.

**3. Novelty, network effects, and category creation resist local testing.** 'Think globally, test locally' breaks for products whose value *only* appears at scale or with a network (a marketplace with no other side, a social network of one, a standard nobody else adopts). A local Fake Door for the telephone, the fax, or Facebook circa 2004 would likely under-read demand. The method is strongest for *additive* products in *existing* categories and weakest for genuinely new behaviors.

**4. The ethics are waved through too quickly.** Fake Door, Infiltrator, and Relabel rely on deception; the 'give them a gift afterward' patch is goodwill, not a framework. 'Don't do it in regulated/medical fields' is the only hard line. For B2B, trust-based, or reputation-sensitive markets, a discovered pretotype can poison the very market you're measuring.

**5. 'Skin in the game' is treated as currency, but conversion ≠ value.** A $1 Kindle price or a refundable $5k deposit measures *willingness to commit at that price/moment*, not lifetime value, unit economics, or retention. The Caliper's clean point-scale (1 email, 10 phone, 1/$) implies a precision and additivity the underlying psychology doesn't have. Twenty preorders can still be a business that loses money on every unit.

**6. Hidden assumption: demand is the dominant risk.** The whole framework presumes Premise is the bottleneck (and FLOP data supports that *on average*). But for deep-tech, biotech, hardware, or infrastructure, the binding constraint is often *Can we build it at all / at cost?*—precisely the prototype question Savoia de-emphasizes. The book is calibrated for software-era, low-build-cost, fast-iteration products, and quietly assumes that profile.

**Net:** an excellent, honest *heuristic toolkit* for cheaply killing bad consumer/software ideas early—but it overclaims as a near-law ('cannot not work'), under-tests its own efficacy, and travels poorly into network, deep-tech, and trust-sensitive domains.
body_md.zh:
萨沃亚有令人耳目一新的自省（他甚至给自己的案例贴上”OPD“和”轶事”的标签），但 INTP 仍应对那些承重节点施压。

**1. 证据库里的幸存者偏差。** 几乎每个被引用的成功（Airbnb、维珍、PalmPilot、CarsDirect、《火星救援》）都是在它*赢了之后*被重构的——”它们做过廉价的早期测试，所以测试导致了成功”。但我们从未看到那些*通过*了预型却仍然失败的产品坟场，或那些*没通过*预型、但放大后本会成功的产品。该方法的命中率是被断言的（”约 80% 保证”），从未被测量。按他自己的标准，本书的核心主张缺乏 YODA。

**2. 预型与市场的错配被低估了。** 预型测的是一个*本地*切片里的*代理*信号。当代理与真实产品分叉时，它既可能是出色的假阴性机器，*也*可能是假阳性机器：谷歌 Glass 通过了一个昂贵的切身投入测试（1500 美元 + 路费），*仍然*失败——萨沃亚承认初始承诺 ≠ 持续参与，却没给出系统性的办法去*事先*判断哪些产品需要*留存型*预型而非*首购型*预型。好奇心购买（Fold4U 的”试了一次”）与真实需求之间，恰恰是最难判读的边界。

**3. 新颖性、网络效应与品类创造抗拒本地测试。**“全局思考，本地检验”对那些价值*只*在规模或网络下才显现的产品会失效（一个没有另一边的市场、一个只有一个人的社交网络、一个无人采纳的标准）。给电话、传真，或 2004 年的 Facebook 做一个本地假门，很可能会低估需求。该方法对*现有*品类里的*增量*产品最强，对真正全新的行为最弱。

**4. 伦理被太快放行。** 假门、渗透者、换标都依赖欺骗；”事后送个礼物”的补丁是善意，不是框架。”别在受监管/医疗领域做”是唯一的硬线。对 B2B、基于信任或对声誉敏感的市场，一个被识破的预型会毒化你正在测量的那个市场本身。

**5.“切身投入”被当作货币，但转化 ≠ 价值。** 1 美元的 Kindle 定价或一笔可退的 5000 美元押金，测的是*在那个价格/那一刻的承诺意愿*，而非终身价值、单位经济或留存。卡尺干净的分数刻度（1 邮箱、10 电话、1/美元）暗示了一种底层心理学并不具备的精确性与可加性。二十笔预订仍可能是一门每卖一件就亏钱的生意。

**6. 隐藏假设：需求是主导风险。** 整个框架假定前提是瓶颈（FLOP 数据*平均*支持这点）。但对深科技、生物技术、硬件或基础设施，约束往往是*我们到底能不能造出来/以可承受的成本造出来？*——恰恰是萨沃亚淡化的那个原型问题。本书是为软件时代、低制造成本、快速迭代的产品校准的，并悄悄假定了这一画像。

**总评：** 一套出色而诚实的*启发式工具箱*，用于廉价地在早期扼杀糟糕的消费/软件想法——但它把自己拔高成近乎定律（”不可能不管用”），对自身效力测试不足，且在网络型、深科技与信任敏感的领域里水土不服。

body_md.en:
A concrete operating checklist. Run it on your *next* idea, not a hypothetical one.

**Step 0 — Adopt the prior.** Write at the top of your plan: *'This idea is presumed to be The Wrong It until my own data proves otherwise.'* Set a target failure assumption of 90%.

**Step 1 — State the MEH in one sentence.** 'How do I assume the market will engage with this?' Don't polish it yet.

**Step 2 — Say it with numbers → XYZ Hypothesis.** Rewrite as **`At least X% of Y will Z`**. Force a number on every fuzzy word ('some', 'cheap', 'a lot', 'interested'). If you're on a team, have each person fill in X, Y, Z privately first—the disagreements *are* the value.

**Step 3 — Hypozoom to an xyz you can test *this week*.** Shrink Y to a small, *local*, reachable subset (your city, your office, one platform, one shop). Keep the sample ~100–1,000 and representative.

**Step 4 — Pick a pretotype.** Match the cheapest technique to your idea:
- Selling something / gauging demand → **Fake Door** (ad or landing page + 'Buy/Notify' button) or **Facade** (actually fulfill the first orders).
- 'Magic tech' you can't build yet → **Mechanical Turk** (a human behind the curtain).
- Will *I* even use it? / form-factor → **Pinocchio** (carry a dummy and pretend).
- Needs to be *seen in action* → **YouTube** (a video + a skin-in-the-game ask).
- Physical retail product → **Infiltrator** / **Relabel** (borrow someone's shelf & traffic).
- Big long-term commitment (lease, fleet) → **One-Night Stand** (one short run first).

**Step 5 — Demand skin in the game.** Design the experiment so success = a *costly* action (a validated email at minimum; ideally a deposit or purchase). Never count views, likes, or survey answers as evidence.

**Step 6 — Optimize the three metrics.** Before launching, ask 'Is this the best I can do?' and push down **DTD** (Distance to Data), **HTD** (Hours to Data—aim <48h), **$TD** (Dollars to Data—aim for 'pizza-budget').

**Step 7 — Score on the TRI Meter.** For each result ask: *'If this were The Right It, how likely is this outcome?'* Map to Very Unlikely → Very Likely. Discard contaminated runs (note *why*). Run **3–5+ experiments**; one is never enough.

**Step 8 — Decide: Go / Tweak / Drop.**
- Arrows cluster Likely/Very Likely *and* outnumber the failure prior → **Go** (now build It right).
- Mixed but you learned something → **Tweak it and flip it** (change price/name/segment/feature; even flip every assumption to its opposite à la Cirque du Soleil) and re-test. Tweaks beat pivots.
- Stubbornly negative across tweaks → **Drop it** and bank what you learned for the next idea.

**Step 9 — Only now write the plan.** Replace projections with collected YODA + skin-in-the-game evidence. *Before writing a business plan, make sure there is a business.*

**Ethics guardrail:** never pretotype in medical/regulated domains where deception harms; reward the people who give you data; prefer Facade over Fake Door when trust matters.
body_md.zh:
一份具体的操作清单。用在你的*下一个*想法上，而不是一个假想的想法。

**第 0 步 —— 接受先验。** 在计划书顶端写下：*“在我自己的数据证明之前，这个想法被推定为错的东西。”* 把失败假设设为 90%。

**第 1 步 —— 用一句话写出 MEH。** “我假设市场会如何参与这个？” 先别打磨。

**第 2 步 —— 用数字说话 → XYZ 假设。** 改写成 **`至少 X% 的 Y 会 Z`**。给每个含糊词（”一些”“便宜”“很多”“感兴趣”）强行配上数字。如果是团队，让每人先私下填 X、Y、Z——那些分歧*就是*价值所在。

**第 3 步 —— 缩放到一个*本周*就能测的 xyz。** 把 Y 缩到一个小的、*本地的*、够得着的子集（你的城市、你的公司、一个平台、一家店）。样本保持约 100–1000 且有代表性。

**第 4 步 —— 挑一个预型。** 把最便宜的技术匹配到你的想法：
- 卖东西 / 探测需求 → **假门**（广告或落地页 + “购买/通知”按钮）或**门面**（真的履行最初几笔订单）。
- 你还造不出的”魔法技术” → **机械土耳其人**（幕后藏个人）。
- 我*自己*到底会不会用？/ 形态 → **匹诺曹**（揣着一个假货假装在用）。
- 需要*被看到运作* → **YouTube**（一段视频 + 一个切身投入的要求）。
- 实体零售产品 → **渗透者** / **换标**（借别人的货架和客流）。
- 重大长期承诺（租约、车队）→ **一夜情**（先来一次短期的）。

**第 5 步 —— 索取切身投入。** 设计实验，使”成功”= 一个*有代价*的动作（最低是验证过的邮箱；理想是押金或购买）。永远不要把观看、点赞或问卷答案当证据。

**第 6 步 —— 优化三项指标。** 启动前先问”这是我能做到的最好吗？”，并压低 **DTD**（到数据的距离）、**HTD**（到数据的小时数——目标 <48 小时）、**$TD**（到数据的金钱——目标是”披萨预算”）。

**第 7 步 —— 在 TRI 仪表上打分。** 对每个结果问：*“如果这是对的东西，这个结果有多可能？”* 映射到极不可能 → 极可能。丢弃被污染的实验（记下*原因*）。跑 **3–5 个以上的实验**；一个永远不够。

**第 8 步 —— 决定：上 / 微调 / 放弃。**
- 箭头聚集在可能/极可能，*且*压过了失败先验 → **上**（现在把它造对）。
- 参半但有所学 → **微调并翻转**（改价格/名字/人群/功能；甚至像太阳马戏团那样把每个假设翻成相反）再测。微调胜过转向。
- 微调后仍顽固为负 → **放弃**，把所学攒下来留给下一个想法。

**第 9 步 —— 到现在才写计划书。** 用采集到的 YODA + 切身投入证据替换预测。*在写商业计划书之前，先确保真的有一门生意。*

**伦理护栏：** 永远不要在欺骗会造成伤害的医疗/受监管领域做预型；回报那些给你数据的人；当信任重要时，优先用门面而非假门。

body_md.en:
**The one line:** *Make sure you are building The Right It before you build It right.*

**The disease → the cure**

| Concept | One-liner |
|---|---|
| **Law of Market Failure** | ~80–90% of new products fail, *even if competently executed* |
| **Success Equation** | `Right A × B × C × … = Success`; one wrong factor (×0) = failure |
| **The Right It / Wrong It** | Right It succeeds if executed; Wrong It fails no matter what. Root cause = **Premise** |
| **FLOP** | Failure from **L**aunch, **O**perations, or **P**remise (Premise dominates) |
| **Thoughtland** | Where ideas attract *opinions, not data* |
| **Four Trolls** | Lost-in-Translation · Prediction · No-Skin · Confirmation Bias |
| **OPD vs YODA** | Other People's Data ≪ **Your Own DAta** (fresh, relevant, sourced, significant) |

**The pipeline:** MEH → *say it with numbers* → **XYZ** (`≥X% of Y will Z`) → *hypozoom* → **xyz** (small/local/now) → **pretotype** → **YODA + skin** → **TRI Meter** → Go / Tweak / Drop.

**Pretotype ≠ Prototype:** prototype = *Can we build it?* · pretotype = ***Should** we build it?* (hours, ~$0).

**The 8 pretotypes:** Mechanical Turk · Pinocchio · Fake Door · Facade · YouTube · One-Night Stand · Infiltrator · Relabel.

**Skin-in-the-Game Caliper:** opinions/likes = **0** · email = 1 · phone = 10 · time = 1/min · money = 1/$. *Money talks, opinion walks.*

**TRI Meter:** 5 bands (Very Unlikely → Very Likely); a black 'Law of Market Failure' arrow presumes guilt; need **3–5+** experiments.

**Tactics + metrics:** Think globally, test locally (**DTD**) · Test now > later (**HTD**, <48h) · Cheap, cheaper, cheapest (**$TD**) · Tweak & flip before you quit (*ten tweaks > one pivot*).

**Worked case — BusU:** $3,000/10-week class = Wrong It (Idea 1); $300/1-week AI class = sells out (Idea 2); ~$40k skin in the game. *Before a business plan, make sure there's a business.*

**3 promises:** flip ~80% fail → ~80% succeed (if executed) · fail without feeling foolish · stick with it and you'll eventually win.
body_md.zh:
**一句话：** *在把东西做对之前，先确保你做的是对的东西。*

**疾病 → 解药**

| 概念 | 一句话 |
|---|---|
| **市场失败定律** | 约 80–90% 的新产品失败，*即便执行得当* |
| **成功方程式** | `对的A × B × C × … = 成功`；一个错误要素（×0）= 失败 |
| **对的/错的东西** | 对的东西执行了就成功；错的东西怎样都失败。根因 = **前提** |
| **FLOP** | 失败源于**发布 L**、**运营 O** 或**前提 P**（前提为主） |
| **思想国** | 想法在此吸引的是*意见，不是数据* |
| **四只小妖** | 翻译走样 · 预测失灵 · 无切身投入 · 确认偏误 |
| **OPD vs YODA** | 别人的数据 ≪ **你自己的数据**（新鲜、相关、来源清楚、显著） |

**流水线：** MEH → *用数字说话* → **XYZ**（`至少 X% 的 Y 会 Z`）→ *缩放假设* → **xyz**（小/本地/现在）→ **预型** → **YODA + 切身投入** → **TRI 仪表** → 上 / 微调 / 放弃。

**预型 ≠ 原型：** 原型 = *我们能造吗？* · 预型 = ***我们该不该**造？*（几小时、约 0 元）。

**8 种预型：** 机械土耳其人 · 匹诺曹 · 假门 · 门面 · YouTube · 一夜情 · 渗透者 · 换标。

**切身投入卡尺：** 意见/点赞 = **0** · 邮箱 = 1 · 电话 = 10 · 时间 = 1/分 · 金钱 = 1/美元。*钱会说话，意见走开。*

**TRI 仪表：** 五档（极不可能 → 极可能）；一支黑色”市场失败定律”箭头推定有罪；需要 **3–5 个以上**的实验。

**战术 + 指标：** 全局思考本地检验（**DTD**）· 现在测胜过以后（**HTD**，<48 小时）· 便宜、更便宜、最便宜（**$TD**）· 先微调翻转再放弃（*十次微调 > 一次转向*）。

**实例 — BusU：** 3000 美元/十周课 = 错的东西（想法 1）；300 美元/一周 AI 课 = 售罄（想法 2）；约 4 万美元切身投入。*写商业计划书之前，先确保有一门生意。*

**三个承诺：** 把约 80% 失败翻成约 80% 成功（若执行到位）· 失败而不觉得自己愚蠢 · 坚持下去你终将取胜。
